## My thinking for this year

I'm 58, been working this land 30 years. My 19.1 mu is split — about 15 mu I do the wheat-maize double crop like most folks in the village, and 4 mu I keep in cotton because the soil on that piece has always done better with cotton and I already have the habit. My wife helps, and one of my kids comes back for harvest, but mostly it's the two of us.

Money is always tight. I don't buy the fanciest inputs, but after 30 years I know what my land needs. The extension guy at the township came by last winter saying 15 kg N per mu for wheat, but honestly I've always done a bit more — maybe 17 or 18 — because my last good wheat crop was when I pushed the topdress a little. I split it: some compound fertilizer as base before planting, then urea at jointing when the wheat wakes up after winter.

For maize I don't have much time to think — the day the combine leaves my wheat field I'm already getting the maize seed in. No plowing, I just direct-seed into the stubble, that's what everyone does now. Saves time, saves money. One base fertilizer at planting, maybe a topdress at big trumpet stage if the plants look pale.

Cotton is more work. I save some seed from last year but also buy some Bt hybrid for the main piece — bollworm used to destroy me before Bt. I hire two neighbors for picking in September because my hands can't keep up anymore at my age.

Irrigation — I have the well but pumping costs real money now with the electric meters. Wheat needs at least the winter water and the jointing water, can't skip those. Maize usually one time if June is dry. Cotton I watch carefully, one or two times depending on the summer rains.

My budget this year is around 8,000 yuan for all inputs. I won't go over. If fertilizer prices jumped again I'd just apply a bit less and hope.
